title: 10 X Sucrose Orange G Loading Dye
author: Gordon Wellman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kp7cvrn
materials: Allow to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Dissolve sucrose in warm water
steps.instruction: Weigh 10 g (for a 25 mL preparation) or 20 g (for a 50 mL preparation) of sucrose and dissolve it completely in 20 mL (for 25 mL) or 40 mL (for 50 mL) of warm sterile water.

steps.title: Add Orange G and adjust volume
steps.instruction: Add Orange G sodium salt (0.05 g for 25 mL or 0.1 g for 50 mL) to the sucrose solution, then add sterile water to bring the total volume to exactly 25 mL or 50 mL, giving a 0.4 % (w/v) Orange G and 40 % (w/v) sucrose solution (10 X loading dye).

steps.title: Aliquot into labeled tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 1 mL of the prepared loading dye into each pre‑labeled 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Store aliquots at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Place the aliquoted tubes at –20 °C; the dye remains stable for years.

steps.title: Defrost and use loading dye
steps.instruction: Fully defrost an aliquot before use; add 1 µL of the 10 X loading dye to every 10 µL of PCR product for gel electrophoresis. Unused portion of the aliquot may be re‑frozen without affecting performance.
